title: Asking About the Past: Mit csináltál?

sections.title: The same question words, a new tense
sections.content: You already ask questions with mit, kivel and miért in the present tense — nothing about their position changes when the verb moves to the past. Mit csinálsz? ("What are you doing?") simply becomes Mit csináltál? ("What did you do?"), with the question word staying right where it always was.

items.english: What did you do yesterday evening?
Who did you talk to at the store?

sections.content: kivel ("with whom") is built from ki ("who") plus -val/-vel, the same instrumental ending you already use for saying who you did something with — Károllyal, Petrával. Answer a kivel question the same way you'd answer any -val/-vel question, just in the past tense.
